## 0d655a5e1a2d

**Issue found: all generated positive motifs are isolated three-cell
components.** Across 600 draws, all 1,694 nonzero connected components had size
exactly 3, and zero qualifying 2x2 L windows were embedded in a larger
component. Therefore this rival fits every sampled generated row and all
canonical examples:

> Fill the missing corner only when the entire connected colored component is
> exactly a three-cell L.

Exact counterexample:

```text
input       authority     rival
220         220           220
200         220           200
200         200           200
```

The upper-left 2x2 window has three 2s and one zero, but it is part of a
four-cell component because of the extra 2 below it. The exact canonical Racket
rule fills the local missing corner; the component-only rival leaves the grid
unchanged. The sampled generator never emits this disambiguating case. The
same census also found 2/600 easy draws with fewer than the documented two L
windows, although `self_check` currently accepts one. Evidence and exact
Racket outputs are retained in `checks/audits/adversarial_census.json`.

## 0d655a5e1a2d

**Issue found: the generator never embeds a qualifying local L inside a larger
same-color component.** This leaves the canonical-fitting rival:

> Fill a missing 2x2 corner only when the three colored cells constitute the
> entire connected component and that component has size exactly 3.

The rival fits all 4/4 canonical train/test pairs. In a fresh 300-draw census,
all 860 nonzero components had size exactly 3, all 860 qualifying L windows were
isolated components, and zero qualifying windows were embedded in a component
larger than 3.

Exact counterexample, verified through the selected Racket authority:

```text
input   Racket authority   component-only rival
220     220                220
200     220                200
200     200                200
```

The upper-left local 2x2 has three 2s and one zero, so the authority fills the
missing corner. The extra 2 below makes a four-cell component, so the rival
incorrectly leaves it blank. The current generator does not emit this
counterexample family. Secondary mismatch: the documented invariant requires
at least two L patterns, while `self_check` accepts one; 4/300 sampled draws had
fewer than two. Evidence: `checks/audits/adversarial_probe.json`.

triage.reason: Both source-bound finding sections retained for future task owners. Local main-generator checks do not independently reproduce these audits. See REVIEW/intake-20261002-batch12.json.

## 0d655a5e1a2d

**Classification: Reproduced defect.** Generator SHA-256 `14ac6af0e103adf597d67eb2bff59d0dfd710146320f223a82f479bfc19e2e21`; canonical rule hash `73f858d8de1d`.

The documented invariant and module description require at least two separated L-trominoes, but `self_check` only requires one. A 6×7 grid containing exactly one same-color three-cell L in a 2×2 window returns no validator errors. The supported canonical Racket rule accepts and transforms that input, so this is specifically a validator/domain mismatch rather than a rule crash.

The advertised `n_l` axis is also dead. With seed `"audit-n-l"`, sample index `0`, `n_l=1` and `n_l=4` produce byte-identical grids containing three detected L windows. The generator chooses its random target without consuming the override.

Reproducer, exact input, validator result, override parameters, actual Racket output, source/rule hashes, and commands: `checks/audit/0d655a5e1a2d/counterexample.json`. Independent lint and defect-lint also fail for missing rule pin/dead axes: `checks/audit-0d655a5e1a2d/lint/` and `checks/audit-0d655a5e1a2d/defect/`.

**Patch status:** audit-only, left unchanged. A task repair should make the invariant and validator agree, then either honor `n_l` exactly or remove/narrow the axis.
